items.e: AND THE LORD SAID UNTO MOSES: HEW THEE. Pesal lekha (hew thee) is similar to lekh lekha (get thee out) (Gen. 12:1) and ve-attah kach lekha (take thou also unto thee) (Ex. 30:23).

[LIKE UNTO THE FIRST.] The same size as the first. Saadiah Gaon says that the second tablets were more precious than the first, for the second tablets were given on a holy day, on the Day of Atonement. This was not the case with the first tablets. The first tablets descended on the seventeenth day of Tamuz, on a weekday. Furthermore, three covenants are mentioned with regard to the second tablets; and that it may go well with thee (Deut. 5:16) was inscribed on the second tablets; and the first tablets were broken. Now these things are similar to that which is seen in a dream. They neither help nor hinder. Both tablets had God’s writing on them. Furthermore, the first tablets were the work of God whereas the second tablets were the work of Moses.
AND BE READY BY THE MORNING, AND COME UP. This is the third time, and each time Moses stayed on the mountain for forty days and forty nights.

AND NO MAN SHALL COME UP WITH THEE. Scripture states, And no man shall come up with thee , because Aaron and his sons ascended and descended the mountain with Moses after God revealed himself to Israel. Aaron also ascended the mountain with Moses before God’s revelation.
THROUGHOUT ALL THE MOUNT. Even somewhere far removed from the place of God’s glory.

AND HE HEWED TWO TABLES OF STONE…AND TOOK IN HIS HAND TWO TABLES OF STONE. It is Hebrew style to speak thus and say, and took in his hand two tables of stone . The verse does not say, and took in his hand the two tables. Our verse is similar to Then the Lord caused to rain upon Sodom and upon Gomorrah brimstone and fire from the Lord (Gen. 19:24). Scripture does not say, “from Himself.” We similarly find Scripture using the phrase the children of Israel five times in one verse. It is elegant to write thus.

AND THE LORD DESCENDED. Some say that and stood refers to the cloud, for God was passing by. Note that the mountain symbolizes the celestial angels who are on a higher level than human beings, as the mountain is higher than the ground.
AND PROCLAIMED THE NAME OF THE LORD. Note, it was the Lord who was proclaiming. God thus taught Moses how to proclaim the name of the Lord.

AND THE LORD PASSED BY. Do not be amazed that the Lord called out, “the Lord,” for God alone is the knower, the content of his thought, and the object of his thought. This is a very difficult concept. Saadiah Gaon says that the first Lord is connected to and proclaimed . Now if this is so, then why didn’t the master of the cantillical notes connect them? Actually, Scripture repeats the Lord’s name twice in our verse in the same manner that it repeats Abraham’s name in Abraham , Abraham (Gen. 22:11); Jacob’s name in Jacob , Jacob (Gen. 46:2); Moses’ name in Moses , Moses (Ex. 3:4). Our verse is to be similarly read. It is written that there are thirteen attributes. Saadiah Gaon said that the Lord’s glorious name is included in the number. If so, then it is not an attribute. He also says that the second time the divine name is mentioned, it means Lord. However, this is an error, for our verse does not read “Lord.” The term Lord is an honorific substitute used by the reader. Rabbi Nissim says that the phrase long-suffering is really two attributes. God is long-suffering to the good and God is long-suffering to the bad. This too is incorrect, for an attribute is not to be added because of a change of persona. Furthermore, God is long-suffering to the wicked, not to the ones who have not sinned against Him. Observe. Ve-nakkeh (clear) is an attribute unto itself. The thirteen attributes end here. According to the plain meaning of the text, ve-nakkeh lo yenakkeh (and that will by no means clear the guilty) (v. 7) is one attribute, for ve-nakkeh (clear) is an infinitive. It is similar to anneh (afflict) in anneh te’anneh oto (if thou afflict them in any wise) (Ex. 22:22). Ve-nakkeh lo yenakkeh teaches that God will by no means clear the rebellious. God forgives only those who repent, as the prophets teach. The word ve-nakkeh was therefore counted as one of the thirteen attributes. The phrase poked avon avot (visiting the iniquity of the fathers) (v. 7) is also an attribute of mercy. Note that there are seven priestly garments. However, the plate was counted among the priestly garments because it is similar to an ornament. Look. Eleven tribes were born in Paddan-aram. Benjamin alone was born in the land of Canaan. However, Scripture writes concerning all of them, These are the sons of Jacob, that were born to him in Paddan-aram (Gen. 35:26). It does so because Scripture speaks of the majority. It is not concerned with excluding the one exception. Scripture similarly states, Thy fathers went down into Egypt with threescore and ten persons (Deut. 10:22). However, Manasseh and Ephraim did not descend to Egypt, for they were born there. Now, they included the Lord’s revered name among the attributes even though it is a proper name. I have already mentioned in the Torah portion Ve-Ellah Shemot that the name YHVH (Lord) is at times an adjective and at times an attribute. The Lord, the Lord ( YHVH YHVH ) are two attributes.
[GOD.] The word El (God) is the third attribute.
MERCIFUL. Rachum (merciful) is the fourth attribute.
AND GRACIOUS. Chanun (gracious) is the fifth attribute.
LONG-SUFFERING. Erekh appayim (long-suffering) is the sixth attribute.
AND ABUNDANT IN GOODNESS. Rav chesed (abundant in goodness) is the seventh attribute. The word rav (abundant) is also connected to the word emet (truth).
TRUTH. Rav emet (abundant in truth) is the eighth attribute.
KEEPING MERCY UNTO THE THOUSANDTH GENERATION. Notzer chesed la-alafim (keeping mercy unto the thousandth generation) is the ninth attribute.
FORGIVING INIQUITY. Nose avon (forgiving iniquity) is the tenth attribute.
TRANSGRESSION. Nose pesha (forgiving transgression) is the eleventh attribute.
SIN. Nose chatta’ah (forgiving sin) is the twelfth attribute.
CLEAR. Ve-nakkeh (and clear) is the thirteenth attribute.
[THE LORD.] The name of the Lord, when an adjective, includes angels and humans, those above and those below.
GOD. The term El (God) means powerful. He wisely does that which is proper.
MERCIFUL. As in Like as a father hath mercy upon his children (Ps. 103:13). He watches over them so that they do not fall.
GRACIOUS. As in for I am gracious (Ex. 22:26), to save the one who falls and is unable to rise.
LONG-SUFFERING. He does not become quickly angry at the wicked.
AND ABUNDANT IN GOODNESS. To the righteous and the wicked.
ABUNDANT IN TRUTH. He fulfills and keeps His word.
KEEPING MERCY. Keeping the mercy of a father to his children, provided that the children are righteous.

FORGIVING INIQUITY. Pay attention to what I am about to say. Look. Scripture writes, be thou strong therefore, and be to a man (I Kings 2:2). But was he not a man? Its meaning can only be, be a famous man of valor. However, Scripture writes, for I am too old to be to a man (Ruth 1:12). Its meaning is, I am too old to be sexually approached by a man, or, I am too old to be a woman to a man, for the speaker was a female. Behold. That I may come into her (Gen 34:21) refers to sexual intercourse, for Rachel was a female. However, that came in to thee this night (Gen. 19:5) does not have the same meaning, for Lot was a man. Now Scripture tells us that one who sins shall bear his iniquity ( ve-nasa avono ) (Lev. 5:1); that is, his sin shall not be forgiven except by the punishment which shall befall him. Ve-nasa (shall bear) has the same meaning as tissa (shalt bear it) in And if thou scornest, thou alone shalt bear it (Prov. 9:12). However, Pharaoh said, Now therefore forgive (sa), I pray thee, my sin only this once (Ex. 10:17), because Moses was a righteous person. The general rule is that Scripture is always expressing approbation when it tells us that someone bears his own sin. The term nasa is used in two ways in reference to sin. One, God will forgive the sinner. In this case it is for the benefit of the one whose sin is forgiven. The second way in which this verb is used is to inform us that some evil person shall bear his sin. Now this term has a negative connotation for the one who must bear his sin, but it has a positive connotation for the one whose sin is forgiven, as in then he shall bear (ve-nasa) her iniquity (Num. 30:16), for the sin will be removed from her and be upon him.

FORGIVING…TRANSGRESSION. Note that pesha (transgression) is a more serious violation than avon (iniquity), for the transgressor removes himself, as it were, from the authority of God. Compare, tifsha (revolted) in then Edom revolted from under the hand of Judah (II Kings 8:22). Now avon (iniquity) is less of a violation than pesha (transgression). It refers to a deliberate violation of God’s command.

[SIN.] The word chatta’ah means sin. Chatta’ah is a noun. It is not like the word chatta’ah (sinful) in ha-mamlakha ha-chatta’ah (the sinful kingdom) (Amos 9:8), for the word chatta’ah in the latter is an adjective. The word chatta’ah (sin) takes in all sins committed in thought and in error; avon relates to violations of the law committed verbally or in deed. Now we looked at the prayer which Moses offered because of the incident of the spies. Moses pronounced the name of the Lord. The latter is a noun. The attributes which follow were stated with regard to this name. Moses did not mention the Lord’s name a second time; that is, he did not mention the adjectival name of the Lord because the Lord wanted to destroy Israel. Moses did not mention El (God) because there was no reason to mention this attribute. He also did not mention rachum (merciful) because the Israelites were not simpletons. Moses did not mention channun (gracious) because no one oppressed Israel and they had no need to cry to God for help. Moses mentioned erekh appayim (slow to anger) because they were wicked. Moses noted that God is plenteous in lovingkindness (ve-rav emet). Its meaning is that God is plenteous in lovingkindness to all. Moses did not mention emet (truth) because they were guilty. Moses mentioned that God forgives avon (iniquity) and pesha (transgression). He omitted chatta’ah (sin) because Israel did not err. Moses included himself among the Israelites and said, and pardon our iniquity (avonenu) and our sin (chattatenu) (v. 9) because of his great humility. Moses did not add the phrase pesha’enu (our transgression) because of his great saintliness, for Moses would not rebel.

AND MOSES MADE HASTE. Those whose heads are empty say that when God said, and unto the fourth generation (v. 7) Moses hastened lest the Lord add, and unto the fifth generation. This is a great error. The mind rebels against the thought that Moses would interrupt the Lord while He was speaking, for if Moses acted in this manner he would have immediately incurred the death penalty. It was only after the voice ceased that Moses hastened to pray. Furthermore, the Decalogue reads the same. Now all of Israel heard this. How then could Moses even think that God would add, unto the fifth generation. There was no need to add “of them that hate Me” because He mentions, and that will by no means clear the guilty .

[AND BOWED.] The word va-yikkod comes from a double root. It is related to the word kadkod (skull). Moses placed his skull on the ground. Va-yikkod follows the paradigm of va-yittom (spent) in and when the money was all spent (Gen. 47:15). Similarly va-yikkedu (then they bowed their heads) (Ex. 4:31) is similar to va-yittemu (were ended) (Deut. 34:8). Pay no heed to those who add roots because of a word’s form. The word yiddemu (they are still) in they are as still as a stone (Ex. 15:16) should be understood in this manner.
AND HE SAID. The meaning of let the Lord, I pray Thee, go in the midst of us is, when we journey, as in And I will walk among you (Lev. 26:12).

FOR IT IS A STIFF NECKED PEOPLE. According to Rabbi Merinus, ki am kesheh oref hu (for it is a stiffnecked people) should be rendered, even though it is a stiffnecked people. Similarly, refa’ah nafshi ki chatati lakh (heal my soul; for I have sinned against Thee) (Ps. 41:5) should be rendered, heal my soul; even though I have sinned against Thee. However, I believe that the meaning of refa’ah nafshi ki chatati lakh is, heal my soul because I confess that I have sinned against Thee and I have become ill because of my sins. The meaning of our verse similarly is: I confess that it is a stiff necked people but pardon [our iniquity and our sin].

AND HE SAID: BEHOLD, I MAKE A COVENANT. This is what for after the tenor of these words I have made a covenant with thee and with Israel (v. 27) refers to. The reference is to the conditions starting from Observe thou (v. 11). It is because of this that I will write a second pair of tablets. The latter shall serve as a document of witness. All of this, namely, that I have forgiven their sin, was because of your honor. I will therefore do marvels for you so that all who see you will marvel, and know that I have placed My glory upon you. The aforementioned is something that I have not wrought since the day that I created heaven and earth. The reference is to the shining of Moses’ face. Observe. Scripture writes that at the time of Moses’ death, unlike the nature of all old people, his eye was not dim, nor his natural force abated (Deut. 34:7).

[SUCH AS HAVE NOT BEEN WROUGHT IN ALL THE EARTH, NOR IN ANY NATION.] Its meaning is, such a thing has been unheard of among the nations. Rabbi Saadiah Gaon explains it as follows: such a thing has not been wrought in the land of Egypt, from which you exited, or among any of the other nations.

OBSERVE THOU. I believe that the Lord is addressing Moses. God is telling Moses to keep these things and to then relate them to the children of Israel. Shemor (observe) is to be taken in the sense of shameru (kept) in They kept His testimonies, and the statute that He gave them (Ps. 99:7), in accordance with the way I have explained it in its place.

[BEHOLD, I AM DRIVING OUT BEFORE THEE.] Your opening words to Israel shall be, behold I am driving out before thee . This section is similar to Behold, I send an angel before thee (Ex. 23:20) and the section which precedes it (Ex. 23:12-19).
[I AM DRIVING OUT.] The word goresh (I am driving out) is a transitive verb in the kal . It is the same case with the word gerushah (one divorced) in A widow, or one divorced (Lev. 21:14).
TAKE HEED TO THYSELF. This verse is similar to Thou shalt not bow down to their gods (Ex. 23:24).
BUT YE SHALL BREAK DOWN THEIR ALTARS. This is similar to but thou shalt utterly overthrow them ( Ibid .).
[A JEALOUS GOD.] Scripture mentions a jealous God here as it does in the Decalogue.

LEST THOU MAKE A COVENANT. This is similar to Thou shalt make no covenant with them, nor with their gods (Ex. 23:32). Our verse adds, lest thou make a covenant…and their daughters go astray as an explanation.
[MOLTEN GODS.] The phrase “the gods of the nations” takes in all idol worship. The reason our verse reads molten gods is because of the golden calf.

[THE FEAST OF UNLEAVENED BREAD.] Scripture mentions the feast of unleavened bread here as it does in an earlier chapter. Look. The feast of unleavened bread serves as a memorial, for Scripture states, for in it thou camest out from Egypt (Ex. 23:15). It is because of this that Scripture mentions the law dealing with the firstling of an ass (v. 20), which is also in memory of the Exodus from Egypt. We similarly find Scripture mentioning laws pertaining to the harvest along with the harvest festival, namely, And when ye reap the harvest of your land, thou shalt not reap the corner of thy field , etc. (Lev. 23:22). It similarly mentions the laws pertaining to the harvest in the Torah portion Kedoshim Teheyu . It is because Passover recalls the Exodus that Scripture mentions, All that openeth the womb is Mine (v. 19).
[THY CATTLE.] The word miknekha (thy cattle) is a feminine here. There are many other nouns that are both masculine and feminine.
SIX DAYS THOU SHALT WORK. Scripture earlier reads similarly.

[IN PLOWING TIME AND IN HARVEST THOU SHALT REST.] Scripture states, in plowing time and in harvest thou shalt rest because human life is dependent principally on these activities. Anan, may his name be erased like a cloud, says that the reference is to sexual relations. Will Anan not be covered with shame? We will grant that it is in the hand of man to plow ( charish ). However, Anan is silent ( yacharish ) with regard to the word harvest.

Scripture does not mention the Sabbatical year in this section. What we ordinarily mean by a full day consists of the movement of the upper sphere from east to west in twenty-four hours. A day of the sun consists of three hundred and sixty-five days and about a quarter of a day, for this is how long it takes the sun to make a circuit from its point of departure in the west until it returns to its place. Those who know the science of the constellations will understand this.

AND THE FEAST OF INGATHERING. Scripture states this in two places. Scripture there reads, at the end of the year (Ex. 23:16) because the end of the year is the beginning of the next year. This is the proof. The sun enters the constellation of Libra close to the tenth day. The new year never occurs after the end of the festival of Sukkot. Scripture therefore reads, at the turn of the year . Do not rely on Samuel’s circuits. Only rely on Rav Ada’s circuit even though it requires two adjustments. One, because the sun at times travels in a longer circuit and at times it travels in a shorter circuit. This difference is not in the sun’s movement, for the sun always travels in a consistent course. Its speed only appears to vary when viewed against a point in the sphere of the constellations. A second adjustment has to be made because of the movement of the epicycle at the head of Aries.
THREE TIMES IN THE YEAR. Scripture mentions the God of Israel in this section because of the incident of the golden calf.

FOR I WILL CAST OUT. Scripture explains in this chapter what it does not mention in the earlier one, for there was no need to mention it in the earlier chapter. Now since God commanded all male Israelites to see His face, and all of Israel is doing His will, the Lord will undoubtedly guard their land from their enemies. Scripture explains this point very clearly.
[NEITHER SHALL ANY MAN COVET THY LAND.] I will make your neighbors so fearful that they will not even covet your land. They certainly will not think of waging war.

THE CHOICEST FIRST-FRUITS OF THY LAND. Scripture reads similarly in the earlier chapter. These are the conditions. From Now these are the ordinances (Ex. 21:1) until And six years (Ex. 23:10) consists of ordinances. The high priest and the judge, namely, the king, are obligated to study them and know them. The obligations of the congregation, which are the same as those noted here, are then mentioned.
AND THE LORD SAID. Even though these things were already written, Moses wrote them again with the Decalogue. This section was therefore written twice.

AND HE WAS THERE. Many think that Moses spent eighty days on the mountain until God gave him the tablets. They are mistaken. On the contrary, the words of our ancient sages are, as I have already noted, correct. Look, Moses spent forty days on the mountain until God gave him the first tablets. Scripture clearly states, and Moses was in the mount forty days and forty nights (Ex. 24:18). Moses himself similarly states, So I fell down before the Lord the forty days and forty nights (Deut. 9:25). Moses then said everything that is recorded in the section starting with the words See Thou sayest unto me (Ex. 33:12). Moses then descended and hewed the tablets and personally brought them up to Mount Sinai. Observe, Scripture states, And the Lord passed by before him (v. 6), and later goes on to say, And he was there with the Lord forty days and forty nights; he did neither eat bread, nor drink water . As was his practice the first time, so was his practice the second time.
AND HE WROTE UPON THE TABLES. God wrote upon the tablets, for Scripture explicitly states, and I will write upon the tables the words that were on the first tables, which thou didst break (v. 1).

THAT MOSES KNEW NOT THAT THE SKIN OF HIS FACE SENT FORTH BEAMS WHILE HE TALKED WITH HIM. The meaning of while He talked with him is, while God talked with him. This occurred because the glory was seen upon Moses’ face. Moses’ face therefore shone like the brightness of the firmament.

[SENT FORTH BEAMS.] The word karan (sent forth beams) is related to the word karnayim (rays) in Rays hath He at His side (Hab. 3:4), for the opening part of the verse explicitly states, And a brightness appeareth as the light . Now since Rays hath He at His side follows, our verse repeats the same idea in different words as is the custom of Scripture. May the bones of Chivi the transgressor be crushed, for Chivi said that Moses’ face turned dry as a horn because he did not eat bread. Chivi similarly explains, and they were afraid (v. 30) as meaning they were afraid because Moses’ face was ugly. Now why did this cursed wretch not open his eyes. A person will only fear to approach someone because there is something strange in him which he has never ever seen before. There is no person who has never looked upon the face of a corpse that does not fear to approach a dead body. Furthermore, if this is the case, why was the veil not always upon the face of Moses? Why did Moses always remove the veil (v. 33) when he spoke with Israel? Did Chivi not see that when Moses was one hundred and twenty years old (Deut. 34:7) his eye was not dim, nor his natural force abated ? This was most certainly so when Moses was eighty years old.
AND WHEN AARON. Who was first in rank.
AND ALL THE CHILDREN OF ISRAEL. The reference is to the leaders with whom it was the practice of Moses to speak. Scripture similarly states, And Moses called unto them (v. 31).
RETURNED UNTO HIM. This shows that they turned away from Moses after they went out to meet him because they were greatly frightened.
AND AFTERWARD. Afterward all the children of Israel who stood at the foot of the mount came near.
AND HE GAVE THEM IN COMMANDMENT. All of the conditions already mentioned.

A VEIL. Masveh (veil) is a garment ( kesut ). Some say that the word suto (vesture) in And his vesture in the blood of grapes (Gen. 49: 11) is similar. Do not be amazed that the vav in masveah is enunciated while the vav is suto is silent, for we find the same with the words avlatah (wickedness) (Hos. 10:13) and olatah (iniquity) (Job 5:16). We similarly find ul yamim (an infant of days) (Is. 65:20) and avilim (urchins) (Job. 19:18); el tokh ha-machneh (within the camp) (Deut. 23:11) and also va-yevatter otam ba-tavekh (and divided them in the midst) (Gen. 15:10). Some say that the light was renewed upon Moses’ face every time Moses came to the tent of meeting and spoke with God. When Moses left the tent the light remained as long as he related God’s words to the children of Israel. When Moses finished speaking he put on the veil, for he knew that the light would depart and his face would return to its prior state. It would be an insult to Moses if the Israelites saw his face without light radiating from it. Moses therefore put on the veil. However, when he came in to speak with God he would remove the veil to receive the light. Rabbi Saadiah Gaon says that the light was not removed from Moses’ face until the day of his death. Therefore Moses’ eye was not dimmed. This is correct. However, Saadiah says that Moses put on the veil so that the Israelites would not be afraid when they quarreled with each other. However, I believe that Moses put on a veil out of respect to the light which God newly created upon his face. He did not want Israel to constantly see it. He wanted them to see it only when he spoke God’s words. He removed the veil when he came into the tent of meeting to speak with God face to face. This is the meaning of But when Moses went in , etc. (v. 34).

AND THE CHILDREN OF ISRAEL SAW THE FACE OF MOSES, THAT THE SKIN OF MOSES’ FACE SENT FORTH BEAMS. Observe. The meaning of and Moses put the veil back upon his face is that Moses always acted in this manner. This was his practice in dealing with the Israelites until the day that God’s glory gathered him to Himself. Moses’ grave is unknown, the Lord being merciful unto him. Blessed is He who chose Moses and placed His holy spirit in him.

Blessed is the most high God Who led his people with might; Through his messenger Whose face shined as the light of the sun. He commanded Moses on the mountain To prepare a tent for his dwelling, as stated in The Torah portion Va-Yakhel .

AND MOSES ASSEMBLED. Moses assembled the people so that all of them would hear, from him, the report about the tabernacle and would donate to its construction. Elleh ha-devarim (these are the words) is to be interpreted as referring to the making of the tabernacle and its vessels. Scripture therefore reads, that ye should do them . This is its meaning: God commanded me that you make what I will tell you. Now even though you are obligated to do heaven’s work, the Lord commanded you to be careful and not do any work on the Sabbath. One who violates this law before witnesses will be put to death by a court of law. Scripture explains elsewhere that he will be stoned.

YE SHALL KINDLE NO FIRE. Since Scripture earlier mentioned with regard to the first and the seventh day of the festival of unleavened bread, no manner of work shall be done in them, save that which every man must eat (Ex. 12:16), namely, that it is permitted to prepare food on these days, it now states with regard to the Sabbath, ye shall kindle no fire to bake bread or to cook meat, for fire is required in preparing all food. Rabbi Saadiah Gaon composed a very important work refuting those who dispute with the ancients regarding the Sabbath lights.
AND MOSES SPOKE. Moses now began to explain to the entire congregation what God had commanded him.

TAKE. The word kechu (take) is the opposite of tenu (give). However, when a mem follows a word from the root lamed, kof, chet , then it has the meaning of give. The meaning of kechu li (take me) in Take me, I pray thee, a little water (I Kings 17:10) is, take for me, take on my account. It is the same case with Take (kechu) ye from among you (me-ittekhem) an offering unto the Lord (la-Adonai).

[WHOSOEVER IS OF A WILLING HEART.] The phrase kol nediv libbo (whosoever is of a willing heart) is irregular. It should be interpreted as if written kol asher nedavo libbo (all whose heart made them willing). We find the same with bi-gedol zero’akha (By the greatness of Thine arm) (Ex. 15:16), which should be interpreted as if written bi-zero’akha ha-gadol (by Thy great arm); and zekher rav tuvekha (the fame of Thy great goodness) (Ps. 145:7), which should be interpreted as if written zekher tuvekha ha-rav (the fame of goodness which is great). Rabbi Joshua says that the vav of libbo is superfluous. It is similar to the vav of chayeto in chayeto sadai (every beast of the field) (Ps. 104:11) and the vav of beno in beno be’or (Balaam the son of Beor) (Num. 24:3).

[LET HIM BRING IT.] After stating let him bring it , Scripture continues to explain, and goes on to say that the reference is to the Lord’s offering . There are many such instances, one of them being, and he hath commanded me, my brother (I Sam. 20:29).

[AND SILVER.] Some say that the word kesef (silver) is etymologically related to the word nikhsefah (yearneth) (Ps. 94:3), and that silver is so called because it is a delight to the eyes. Nechoshet (brass) is also so called because women practice magic ( me-nachashot ) with brass ( nechoshet ).

AND SCARLET. The word shani (scarlet) is here spelled without a mem . We also find it spelled with a mem . Compare shanim (scarlet) in Though your sins be as scarlet (Is. 1:18). Perhaps the latter is a plural.
AND SKINS. The word orot (skins) is masculine. Luchot (tables) is similar. So is bechorot (firstlings) in and the firstlings of…thy flock (Deut. 14:23).
ACACIA-WOOD. Shittim (acacia), like the word nashim (women), is spelled with a mem .

AND OIL. Scripture does not mention pure beaten olive oil because this is known. Scripture therefore reads la-ma’or (for the light), as is the custom. Moses now mentioned that those who were “willing-hearted” should bring their offerings. He then went on to say that those who were certain that they were experts in the crafts should come and make [all that the Lord hath commanded]. Moses began with the tabernacle because it takes in everything. The tent served as its cover. He then mentions its covering . Its covering takes in the two coverings.
ITS CLASPS. The clasps of the tabernacle and the tent.
ITS BARS, ITS PILLARS, AND ITS SOCKETS. The pillars for the veil and the screen. Scripture then mentions the holy vessels which were placed behind the veil.
AND THE SHOWBREAD. For the table was constructed for the showbread.
THE CANDLESTICK. Scripture mentions the oil for the light because the menorah was made for it.

AND THE ALTAR. Scripture concludes the account of the holy vessels. It then mentions the screen for the door. Now the vessels of the oil for the lighting, and the vessels of the anointing oil and the sweet incense, shall be placed between the veil and the screen of the door of the tabernacle because they are holy.
THE LAVER AND ITS BASE. Observe, the laver and its base had no staves. It is possible that they were carried on wagons.

THE HANGINGS OF THE COURT, THE PILLARS THEREOF ( AMMUDAV ), AND THEIR SOCKETS ( ADONEHAH ). Our verse is similar to and a great (gedolah) and strong (chazak) wind (ru’ach) (I Kings 19:11) and to A fire (esh) not blown (nuppach) by man shall consume him (te’okhlehu) (Job 20:26).
THE PLAITED GARMENTS. Necessary for the journey.
DEPARTED. We learn from this that the entire congregation of Israel came to the tent of meeting group by group.
AND THEY CAME, EVERY ONE WHOSE HEART STIRRED HIM UP. The reference is to the wise-hearted. The meaning of nesa’o libbo (whose heart stirred him up) is, whosoever had an exalted heart.

MEN AND WOMEN. The meaning of al nashim (and women) is, with women. Al here is similar to al (with) in with (al) the bread of the first-fruits for a wave-offering (Lev. 23:20). There are many other such instances.

AS MANY AS WERE WILLING-HEARTED. Nediv lev (willing-hearted) includes willing-hearted women. The term is used in the same sense as ha-shafan (and the rock-badger) (Lev. 11:5) and shor seh khevasim (the ox, the sheep) (Deut. 14:4).
NOSE-RINGS. Chach is an earring.
AND EAR-RINGS. Nezem is a nose-ring.
AND SIGNET-RINGS. Taba’at (signet-ring) is a ring which is placed on the finger.
AND GIRDLES. Kumaz (girdle) is a ring which is placed around the arm.
AND EVERY MAN. Or woman. In addition, the women spun the blue and the purple, the scarlet, the fine linen and also the goats’ hair, a craft which required exceptional skill.

AND THE RULERS BROUGHT THE ONYX STONES, AND THE STONES TO BE SET. They had these items because when Israel left Egypt and despoiled the Egyptians, every Israelite asked for articles in accordance with his status. Now it was truly a great thing that the rulers possessed oil for the light many months after Israel left Egypt. Scripture next mentions the men and women together and backtracks and speaks of the women whose heart stirred them up to do the work. It mentions the chief, whom all should obey because there is no one as wise as he among them.
AND HE HATH FILLED HIM. Look. God bore witness that Bezalel was saturated with wisdom, understanding, and knowledge, and in addition was skilled in all manner of workmanship.

AND TO DEVISE SKILFUL WORKS. Ve-la-chashov machashavot (and to devise skilful works) is to be interpreted as meaning: and to devise in his heart designs which were never seen. [IN GOLD, AND IN SILVER.] For some people are skilled in working with gold but not in working with silver. Others are skilled stone masons but are not skilled wood carvers. However, Bezalel was a master of all of these crafts.

[AND HE HATH PUT IN HIS HEART THAT HE MAY TEACH.] In addition to the above, God put in his heart the ability to teach because there are many wise men who teach with great difficulty. Now Oholiab was Bezalel’s colleague in all the crafts and in the skill of teaching to others. Scripture therefore says with regard to both of them, even of them that do any workmanship, and of those that devise skilful works (v. 35).
SHALL WORK. Look. Bezalel himself shall make the glorious object. However, he and Oholiab shall teach.

CALLED. The heh of the word le-korvah (to come) is superfluous. It is like the heh in the word u-le-dovkah (and to cleave) in and to cleave unto Him (Deut. 11:22). A great scholar erred in saying that the word le-omdah (it might stand) (Ezek. 17:14) is similar, for the heh in le-omdah has a mappik in it. Omed is an intransitive verb. The meaning of le-omdah (it might stand) is therefore to stand by it.
AND THEY RECEIVED. All the offering which they had brought.
AND THEY. The Israelites continued to bring free-will offerings to Moses every morning.
AND ALL THE WISE MEN…CAME. To Moses’ tent and said, The people bring much more [ than enough for the service of the work ] (v. 5).

[MUCH MORE THAN ENOUGH.] The mem of mi-de (much more than enough) means: much more than. It is, in keeping with my interpretation, like the mem of mi-kol (more than all) in I have more understanding than all my teachers (Ps. 119:99).
AND THEY CAUSED IT TO BE PROCLAIMED. Va-ya’aviru (and they caused to be proclaimed) is similar to va-ya’avor (and there went) in And there went a cry throughout the host (I Kings 22:36).
FOR THE STUFF. The work which was done.
[SUFFICIENT.] The mem of dayyam (sufficient) refers to all of the wise men.
FOR ALL THE WORK. That they had to do.
AND TOO MUCH. Ve-hoter (and too much) is an infinitive. Its meaning is, ho-tirah (and they produced more than enough).
MADE. Scripture begins with the making of the tabernacle.

TWINED. Moshzar (twined) means long in Arabic. Note that the single digit numbers are grammatically irregular in Hebrew. This is also the case in Aramaic. They are similarly irregular in Arabic. The heh at the end of a word indicates the feminine; the masculine does not have any sign. Now the heh in the number sheloshah (three) indicates the masculine. The same is true of the numbers arba’ah (four), shemonah (eight), asarah (ten). From there through twenty the masculine numbers do not have a heh at the end. We thus say achad asar (eleven), shenem asar (twelve), tishah asar (nineteen). The feminine is written with a heh . However, its vocalization is changed so that it reads esreh . This is done so that the word not be confused with the masculine. Hence we say shetem esreh (twelve). The same applies to all of the numbers. Look. Shalosh (three), arba (four), and eser (ten) are feminine. If their sum is in the construct then it ends in a tav both in the masculine and in the feminine. Compare, sheloshet ha-anashim ha-elleh (these three men) (Ezek. 14:16); and u-sheloshet neshe vanav (and the three wives of his sons) (Gen. 7:13). Now the masculine form for the number eight is shemonah , as the rule says. The feminine is unique in that one says shemoneh (eight) in the same way that one says ashte esreh (eleven).
[CUBITS.] It is possible that the reason our verse reads ba-ammah (cubits) is that it refers to a specific cubit. It possibly refers to the noble cubit of the first temple.

[THE LOOPS.] The tav of ha-lula’ot (the loops) indicates the feminine. The singular form of the word is lulah . The heh [in lulah ] takes the place of the alef . Some say that the word lalat (near to be delivered) in was with child, near to be delivered (I Sam. 4:19) comes from the same root.
FOR THE TENT. La-ohel (for tent) means to serve as a tent.

[TO PASS THROUGH.] The word livro’ach (to pass through) is a kal . It has the same meaning as the hifil mavri’ach (pass through). We find the same with the words yereh (shoot) and va-yoreh (and he shot) (II Kings 13:17). There are many such instances.

AND BEZALEL MADE. Bezalel made the ark because of its importance. Bezalel also made all the holy vessels. Now Scripture mentions the tabernacle, the tent, the veil, and the screen, for they serve a similar purpose. Scripture then mentions the holy anointing oil with the incense of sweet spices because there are spices in the anointing oil and also in the sweet incense.

[OF THE MIRRORS.] Be-marot (of the mirrors) has a bet rather than a mem prefaced to it. It is proper Hebrew to do so. We find the same in the verse ve-ha-notar ba-basar u-va-lachem (and that which remaineth of the flesh and of the bread) (Lev. 8:32). It is the same case in Arabic.

[THAT DID SERVICE.] Scripture states this because it is the custom of all women to beautify themselves. They look at their faces in brass or glass mirrors every morning to arrange the head coverings upon their heads. These head coverings are mentioned in the Book of Isaiah. The custom of Israel was the same as the Moslem practice unto this very day. Now there were in Israel women who served God and removed themselves from the pleasures of this world. These women gave their mirrors as a free-will offering because they had no need to beautify themselves. They rather came daily to the door of the tent of meeting to pray and to hear the words of the commandments. Scripture states, that did service (tzave’u) at the door of the tent of meeting because there were many such women.
[THE LAVER.] Scripture does not mention the dimensions of the laver as it does in the case of the lavers that Solomon made. The laver was rather made out of all the mirrors that were brought.
[THE BASE.] The ken , that is, the base, was in all instances the same size as the laver as is normally the case.

AND FOR THE WEST SIDE. Scripture refers to the west as the hinder part because the tent’s opening was on the east, which is referred to as the face. Scripture refers to the sides which were close to the door as shoulders, for they are compared to the shoulders of a human being.
Give thanks to God and ascribe power to Him O “Father of a multitude,” Now that you have reached the opening of the Torah portion Ellah Pekude .

THESE ARE THE ACCOUNTS OF THE TABERNACLE. Its meaning is: these are the accounts of the vessels of the tabernacle, for the word tabernacle includes everything. Scripture goes on to explain why the structure was referred to as a mishkan (tabernacle). It was so called because the tablets of testimony were placed in it. Now Scripture was brief. The tablets were truly a testimony, because God’s writing was inscribed upon them.

[THROUGH THE SERVICE OF THE LEVITES.] Its meaning is: through the service of the Levites who carry the tabernacle and all of its vessels which Ithamar appointed to them. For the Gershonites and the Merarites were the Levites under the direction of Ithamar, who listed all the objects they were assigned to carry.
AND BEZALEL. Scripture notes that Bezalel and Oholiab, who were first in rank, executed all of their tasks properly.

ALL THE GOLD. Saadiah Gaon asks, “Why does Scripture note what was done with the silver but does not mention what the donated gold was used for?” He answers, “Look. Scripture notes that the menorah was made out of a talent of gold. This was also the case with the ark cover and the gold utilized for the ark and the altar of incense.” Now this is incorrect. Only the menorah was entirely made of gold. This was not the case with the ark. The ark was only overlaid with gold on the inside and on the outside. The same was true of the altar of incense. The table, the staves, the boards, and the bars were all overlaid with gold. The ark cover was made completely of gold. According to the tradition passed on to us by our fathers the ark cover was made from a talent of gold because it was very broad and very wide. I believe that Scripture mentions what they did with the silver because the silver was given for atonement. Observe. Scripture notes that the tabernacle, which included all the vessels, stood on the silver which the Israelites were obligated to give. This served as a memorial for the children of Israel. Who can estimate how much gold was needed to overlay all the vessels of the tabernacle?
AND THE SILVER. Look. We learn from the sum mentioned in this verse that a talent consists of three thousand shekalim . And the silver of them that were numbered of the congregation proves this.
A BEKA. Half a shekel. Its meaning is: when the shekel will be broken, behold its half.
FOR EVERY ONE THAT PASSED. All those that passed twenty complete years. I have already explained the reason for this.
FOR CASTING. La-tzeket (for casting) comes from a root whose first letter is a yod . It is similar to the word la-redet (to descend).
AND OF THE THOUSAND SEVEN HUNDRED SEVENTY AND FIVE SHEKELS. Which did not serve to complete a talent.
AND THE BRASS. Scripture also mentions the brass vessels.

PLAITED GARMENTS. These garments are the ones that are mentioned in the Torah portion Be-Midbar Sinai (in the wilderness of Sinai). God commanded that the ark be covered with the veil as a mark of honor. A sealskin covering was placed over the veil. A blue cloth covering was placed over this covering. Logically speaking, the blue cloth covering was employed as an ark covering as a mark of honor when the weather was clear. However, if it rained then they would remove the blue cover and they would place a sealskin cover over it. A blue cloth and a cloth of scarlet were placed over the table of showbread. A cover of sealskin was placed over them. A blue cloth was placed over the menorah and the golden altar. A purple cloth was placed over the altar. A sealskin was placed over all of them. After mentioning the plaited garments Scripture mentions the holy garments of Aaron the high priest and then commences to describe them.
AND HE MADE THE EPHOD. Scripture describes how they placed the gold amidst the blue.
[AND THEY WROUGHT THE ONYX STONES.] The meaning of va-ya’as (and they wrought) is, they set. It is like the word la’asot (to dress) in and he hastened to dress it (Gen. 18:7).
[ALL OF BLUE.] Kelil tekhelet means entirely of blue. The word kelil is in the construct.
AND THE MITRE OF FINE LINEN. Worn by Aaron.
AND THE GOODLY HEAD-TIRES. Which were worn by Aaron’s sons. The mitre and the head-tire differ.
THUS WAS FINISHED. Va-tekhel (thus was finished) is vocalized like the word ve-terev (was so much) in but Benjamin’s portion was so much (Gen. 43:34).

AND THEY BROUGHT THE TABERNACLE. Look. Et metarav vi-yetedotehah (the cords thereof, and the pins thereof) (v. 40) is similar to et kale he-chatzer et ammudav ve-et adonehah (the hangings of the court, the pillars thereof, and their sockets) (Ex. 35:17).

ON THE FIRST DAY. We find the following difference of opinion. Some say that the eighth day of consecration fell on the first day of the month of Nisan. They were forced to say that Moses erected the tabernacle on the twenty-third day of Adar. Now on the first day of consecration Moses took the tabernacle apart and put it together in order to train the priests. They say that the goat that Moses inquired about and, behold, it was burnt (Lev. 10:16) was a new moon offering. Now God commanded that Moses erect the tabernacle on the first day of the first month and that he not take it apart until the ark journeyed. Now we find it stated in the Sifre that Mishael and Elzaphan were the ones who were unclean by the dead body of a man (Num. 9:6). The eighth was thus the eighth day of the month. There is, as it were, proof of this. First of all, why didn’t Scripture mention that Moses set up the tabernacle and took it apart? After the tabernacle was taken down there was no door of the tent of meeting. However, Scripture states, And at the door of the tent of meeting shall ye abide day and night (Lev. 8:35). Furthermore, Scripture writes, And unto the children of Israel thou shalt speak, saying: Take ye a he-goat for a sin-offering (Lev. 9:3). It was this he-goat that Moses inquired about. Additionally, if this was a goat that served as a new moon offering, why didn’t Scripture mention two bullocks, one ram, and seven he-lambs? Scripture should have read, beside the burnt offering of the new moon, as it does when it states, beside the burnt-offering of the morning (Num. 28:23). Look. According to the plain meaning of the text, the tabernacle was first erected on the first day of the first month. Observe, they raised up this first tabernacle on the first day of the first month. They began to build the first temple, which was the second tabernacle, on the second day of the second month, called Iyyar, as Scripture clearly states, in the second day of the second month (II Chron. 3:2). Our Talmud writes that Israel left Egypt on the fifth day of the week. If they transmitted this as a tradition then we will accept it. However, if we analyze the text logically then we must conclude that they left Egypt before the fifth day of the week because there is at least three days’ difference between a simple year and the beginning of the next year. This is so because a defective year consists of three hundred and fifty-three days, three hundred and fifty of which are taken up by weeks. In minimal leap years there is a difference of five days. Now it appears that Moses arranged the bread on the table on a Sabbath, for Scripture states, Every sabbath day he shall set if in order (Lev. 24:8). The tabernacle was thus erected either on the sixth day or on the Sabbath day. This appears to be the case even though the proof just offered is not irrefutable, for one can argue that the meaning of every sabbath he shall set it in order is, every Sabbath the priest shall set it in order after the tabernacle has been raised and Moses has arranged the bread. Observe. In describing the actual erecting of the sanctuary, Scripture tells that Moses raised up the tabernacle. He erected, as I have explained, the two corner boards. The Levites who were of his family set up the rest of the tabernacle, for it was not the work of one person. He laid its sockets below. He then set the boards and bars in place. He then raised up the pillars for the veil and the screen of the door of the tabernacle. Afterwards Moses spread the tent and put the covering of the tent over it. He then placed the ark on the western side and placed the tablets in the ark. He set the staves on the ark and placed the ark cover on top of the ark. Moses put in the table and arranged the showbread upon it. Now Scripture indicates that this took place in the morning. Scripture states, and he lighted the lamp s(v. 25) afterwards at night. Moses offered the burnt offering in the morning, that is, the daily burnt offering. He did the same in the afternoon. On this day Moses anointed the tabernacle and all of its vessels, the altar of the burnt offering and all of its vessels, the laver and its base. The congregation was gathered at the door of the tent of meeting and Aaron and his sons washed themselves with water. Moses placed the holy garments upon Aaron. He also dressed Aaron’s sons. They were anointed with the holy oil. He brought one young bullock and two rams to the altar. He sacrificed the bullock and performed purification on the altar. He caused the designated parts to turn into smoke and slaughtered the ram. He dashed its blood on the altar and caused the ram to turn into smoke. He also slaughtered the ram of consecration and dashed its blood on the altar. He took the designated parts along with the right thigh and one unleavened cake and one cake of oil bread and turned all of it into smoke on the altar. Moses did this on each one of the seven days of consecration. Scripture clearly writes, And thou shalt offer the bullock of sin-offering to the day …(Ex. 29:36), that is, daily,… and you shall anoint the altar, to sanctify it . Scripture further writes, Seven days thou shalt make atonement for the altar (Ex. 29:37) and thou shalt anoint it, to sanctify it (Ex. 29:36). Now its meaning is, Thus shall you do all the seven days of consecration. Scripture states, And it came to pass on the day that Moses had made an end of setting up the tabernacle, and had anointed it and sanctified the altar for seven days of consecration (Num. 7:1). The princes of Israel then began to bring the dedication offering of the altar. Aaron similarly offered a bull-calf as a personal sin offering, and he also offered his own ram as a burnt offering. As the people’s burnt offering he sacrificed a calf and a lamb. Aaron slaughtered the goat of the sin offering and treated it as a sin offering. He dealt with it as he did with his own calf sin offering with regard to dashing its blood and causing the designated parts to go up in smoke. However, a priest does not eat the priest’s sin offering. The flesh of the bullock was therefore burned outside the camp. The sin offering of the congregation, which is a he-goat, is eaten by the priests. All of this took place after the morning burnt offering was offered. After all of this, he [Aaron] offered the burnt offering and sin offering of Nahshon. The dedication of the altar was thus finished after nineteen days of the first month had passed. Do not pay attention to the one who argues, “If this is the case then when did they offer the festival sacrifices?” Israel observed the festival of Passover in the desert of Sinai for only one night. They did not keep the festival of unleavened bread, for Scripture clearly states, And it shall be when the Lord shall bring thee [ into the land of the Canaanite ] (Ex. 13:5)… Seven days thou shalt eat unleavened bread (Ex. 13:6). And this day shall be unto you for a memorial (Ex. 12:14) refers to the next generation. It commands the next generation to establish the day that Israel left Egypt, as a holy convocation. Look! They journeyed from Goshen on the first day. Furthermore, Israel did not have bread from which to make unleavened bread for seven days in the desert of Sinai even though they were close to an inhabited place. It was a great thing that they found material out of which to make unleavened bread to eat with the bitter herbs and paschal lamb on the one night, for they were a very great multitude of people. Now logically speaking, Moses offered the daily burnt offering during the seven days of consecration and two lambs on the Sabbath day. He offered the Sabbath burnt offering and then the consecration burnt offerings on which day of the seven days of consecration fell on a Sabbath. All of this is correct. However, what shall we do with the dedication of the altar on the Sabbath day? Some say that they skipped the Sabbath day. They only counted the days that they dedicated the altar. Others say that the princes’ burnt offering was offered on the Sabbath. However, the peace offerings were slaughtered and eaten on the first day of the week. Their proof is as follows. The prince who sacrifices offers six lambs on the Sabbath aside from the congregation’s burnt offering. The first group says that when they circled Jericho for six days with the armed body in the lead they similarly skipped the Sabbath. Behold, they circled Jericho for seven days. They say the same with regard to the fourteen days. They skipped the Day of Atonement and did not count it.
THEN THE CLOUD COVERED. Logically speaking, when the tabernacle was erected and Moses went out, the cloud covered the tabernacle and the glory of the Lord filled it.

AND MOSES WAS NOT ABLE TO ENTER. Then God called Moses and told him to enter the tent. Moses used to speak with God face to face in the place where the high priest entered once a year with a cloud of incense, because Moses was, as it were, a member of the house. I was forced to say this because Moses put the tablets in the ark. He similarly placed over the ark the covering with the cherubim on top. God’s glory was always upon them. Now what happened when Aaron and his sons took down the veil of the screen outside the place where the ark was kept? How did they approach it? I therefore say that Moses alone entered beyond the veil. Aaron and his sons then took down the screen, which is called the veil. Moses used to take the screen and immediately cover the ark of the covenant with it so that Aaron and his sons would not see it. Scripture writes, and they shall cover the ark of testimony (Num. 4:5) because they assisted Moses. Others say that the priests covered the ark but did not face it. Scripture states, and there was fire therein by night , and then goes on to say, throughout all their journeys (v. 38). This also indicates that at times the cloud journeyed at night. Now we do not find it written that they journeyed at night. The one who says this explains or if it continued by day and by night (Num. 9:21) as referring to one day. Now what will they do with the phrase their journeys (v. 38)? Scripture does not read: throughout all their encampments. The correct meaning of or…by day and by night is: or day and night; or: or day or night. It is similar to And he that curseth his father and his mother , shall surely be put to death (Ex. 21:17). I had to say this because I noticed that the prayer which Moses uttered on the occasion of the scouts states, and thou goest before them, in a pillar of cloud by day, and in a pillar of fire by night (Num. 14:14).
